title: His mother's name and talk of Indian ancestry among musicians
summary: He gives his mother's name, Leona McBee, and the Dances discuss Indian blood in Ellington, Blanton and Pettiford and a possible Indian contribution to jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, you have some Scottish blood in there too, haven't you?

You know, I was talking to Duke Ellington's sister and she said there was Indian blood on his father's side. (Inaudible). But there's a lot of -- I think (inaudible) -- you know, there were so many people like Jimmy Blanton and Oscar Pettiford -- they were all supposed to have it.

Well, Oscar Pettiford, from what I understand, the Pettiford family, they had Indian blood. Now, they were from, if I make no mistake, I think it was Okmulgee, Oklahoma, and that's only about 30 miles from Muskogee.

Well, the reason we are interested in it, it seems possible that even in this music, there is an Indian contribution that has never really been -- you know, they talk of the racial thing and how it affects the nature of the music and it seems possible that there is an Indian thing in there, too, that has never been recognized, you know?
